record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.context_brief: reinjection near marginally unstable periodic orbits
record.original_question: For stadium-like billiards containing marginally unstable periodic orbits, can one comprehensively characterize their dynamical properties, including escape properties, in terms of reinjection dynamics, meaning the way trajectories that leave the neighborhood of such periodic orbits are returned to that neighborhood?

evidence.quote: One source of interest and also difficulty with the stadium is the fact that orbits that leave the bouncing ball region are immediately reinjected back

Open problem 9. Give a comprehensive characterisation of the dynamical (including escape) properties of marginally unstable periodic orbits in stadium-like billiards in terms of their reinjection dynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a stadium-like planar billiard table, i.e. a bounded domain whose boundary consists of two parallel straight segments joined by two focusing (e.g. circular) arcs, and consider the associated billiard flow (a point particle moving in straight lines inside $Q$ and reflecting elastically off $\partial Q$) together with its Poincaré (collision) map on the boundary phase space. Such a table possesses a one-parameter family of "bouncing-ball" periodic orbits, which are marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs): orbits whose linearized Poincaré map is parabolic (eigenvalues equal to $1$), so that nearby trajectories drift away polynomially rather than exponentially. A trajectory that leaves a small neighborhood $U$ of such a MUPO eventually returns to $U$; the induced first-return map from $U^c$ back to $U$ is called the reinjection map, and the statistics of return positions, return times, and angles constitute the reinjection dynamics.

Now place a "hole" (an open subset of $\partial Q$ or of the phase space) and consider the open billiard: study the survival probability $P(t)=\mu\{x:\text{the trajectory of }x\text{ has not entered the hole by time }t\}$ and related escape quantities (escape rate, asymptotic decay law, conditionally invariant measures).

Problem. Provide a comprehensive characterization of the dynamical properties of MUPOs in stadium-like billiards — in particular the asymptotic behavior of $P(t)$ and other escape statistics for the corresponding open systems — purely in terms of the reinjection dynamics, i.e. derive the escape law, its prefactors, and the structure of conditionally invariant measures from quantitative properties (distribution of return times, return locations, and angles) of the reinjection map associated with the MUPO family.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about giving a complete characterization of escape and other dynamical properties of MUPOs in stadium-like billiards in terms of reinjection dynamics. Searches return work establishing the prevalence of MUPOs and partial results on escape (e.g., polynomial decay of survival probability, rotating leaks in the stadium), but no comprehensive characterization in terms of reinjection dynamics appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Prevalence of marginally unstable periodic orbits in chaotic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the prevalence of a fundamental structure formed by marginally unstable periodic orbits in chaotic billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes prevalence and basic dynamical role of MUPOs but does not give a full characterization via reinjection.

status_evidence.title: Rotating leaks in the stadium billiard
status_evidence.snippet: Studies escape through moving holes in the stadium billiard.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on escape in open stadium billiards exist but the comprehensive characterization remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Marginally Unstable Periodic Orbits in Semiclassical Mushroom Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Treats MUPOs and their interaction with chaotic modes in mushroom billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Related MUPO analyses exist, but a full reinjection-based theory for stadium-like billiards is not provided.
